content:
maria: perf-bot alerted p99 latency spike in serving-prod after v5.2 rollout in us-west-2. p50 up ~8ms, p99 up ~220ms. throughput dropped on several host shards. anyone oncall?
perf-bot: [automated] p99 latency +3.8x vs baseline across model-group/gpt-open-v5.2, affected nodes: node-13,node-14,node-21. auto-flagged for investigation.
ash: oncall here. cron tracing now, attaching initial qps/latency snapshot.
maria: thanks ash. Sam can you pull a perf profile for node-13? suspect kernel selection change after the new build.
sam: grabbing profile now: runtimesctl profile --node node-13 --since 900s --format=flame > /tmp/flame-1768000000.svg
sam: quick flame readout: attention_gemm 46%, memcpy (host<->device) 19%, kernel-launch overhead 9%, batch-aggregation 8%, kv_lookup 6%, tokenizer_split 5%, others 7%.
lee: odd tokenizer_split showing up — what changed in the v5.2 tokenizer? I recall a tweak landed last week.
maria: v5.2 switched to a byte-level BPE fallback for non-ascii which increased split tokens for some payloads. avg_seq_length jumped: baseline 128 -> canary samples ~340 (long-tail).
devin: long seqs explain attention_gemm dominating (O(L^2)). but why did kv_lookup drop? I would expect more cache hits if prefixes were conserved.
sam: KV cache miss rate went up. sampling KV hitrates from traces: pre-rollout ~72% -> post ~28%. logs show tokenization boundaries changed so KV cache keys (which include tokenized prefixes) don't match and prefix reuse vanished.
ash: so two correlated factors: longer sequences (more raw GPU work) AND KV cache fragmentation (more effective work). also noisy tenant on node-14 had a big batch storm at 10:12 UTC which aggravated the tail.
maria: can we confirm batching heuristics led to a different kernel being chosen? runtime kernel selector currently: pick tiled_attention_v1 when avg_seq < 200, otherwise generic_gemm. v5.2 changed the seq distribution so selector fell into generic_gemm, but GPU would perform better with tiled_attention_v2 which selector doesn't pick (v2 was feature-flagged off).
sam: paste from selector code:
```
if seq_len_mean < 200 and batch_tokens < 65536:
    kernel = tiled_attention_v1
else:
    kernel = generic_gemm
```
v5.2 telemetry: seq_len_mean ~340 -> else branch. tiled_attention_v2 exists but not considered.
lee: tiled_attention_v2 reduces memory copies and uses a preallocated workspace — better for long sequences. seems safe to enable as an override.
devin: immediate mitigations:
- force kernel override to tiled_attention_v2 on affected nodes
- cap max_batch_tokens to avoid huge GEMM runs
- route detected long-seq requests to a dedicated long-seq pool
- roll back tokenizer change in canary

ash: plan for now: 1) Sam, push kernel override on node-13/14/21. 2) Maria, pause the v5.2 canary and stop further rollouts. 3) Lee, create tokenizer diff to help normalize KV keys.
sam: applying override: runtimesctl set-config --node node-13,node-14,node-21 --set runtime.kernel_preference=tiled_attention_v2 && runtimesctl restart runtime
sam: post-override flame after 2m: attention_gemm 31%, memcpy 12%, kernel-launch 6%, kv_lookup 12%, batch-agg 10%.
ash: p99 decreased from ~220ms -> ~95ms on those nodes. throughput recovered ~+18%.
maria: kv hitrate also recovered partially (28% -> ~52%) after partial normalization; token boundaries still differ but v2's memory layout helped.
lee: medium-term: we need a tokenizer->KV-key stable mapping layer. proposal: canonicalize KV keys using byte-offset based prefix hashing rather than token ids to decouple tokenizer changes from cache keys.
devin: agree. also add a fuzz test that runs different tokenizers against top customer prompts and measures KV key churn. run against top-50 prompts.
maria: action items / owners:
- sam: keep kernel override until rollout is verified, update selector to prefer tiled_attention_v2 for seq_mean <= 512 (ETA 2d)
- lee: design KV key canonicalization and tokenizer diff tool (ETA 5d)
- devin: create synthetic load to validate batching heuristics and max_batch_tokens safeguards (ETA 3d)
- ash: keep canary paused and coordinate rollback with deploy-bot
- perf-bot: post hourly p99/p95/p50 telemetry for model-group/gpt-open-v5.2 and compare to v5.1

sam: opened hotfix PR to runtime-selector to change threshold and include v2 as an option. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime-selector/pulls/189
maria: will review. after merge we can remove node-level override and let selector manage it.
deploy-bot: paused rollout job id=deploy-5543 per request from ash at 10:22 UTC.
ash: note: noisy tenant on node-14 being investigated by eng-sre; tagging them for follow-up.
devin: also adding a regression test in the canary pipeline: synthetic mixed-unicode sequences to catch tokenization regressions that hurt KV hit.
maria: good. please add to canary matrix.
lee: cost note: longer sequences + extra GEMM runtime increases billable token cost by ~2.5x for those requests. finance should be scoped if we keep v5.2.
maria: thanks all. I'll write a short postmortem after stabilization. closing thread when p99 stable <80ms for 1h.
nash: closing loop: p99 stabilized ~40-60ms cluster-wide after selector fix and rollback. leaving follow-ups in tracker.
